validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED by two independent trade outlets. The gem.wiki page's ONLY citation is 'OPEC Annual Statistics Bulletin 2012 p.75', a generic country-level source that does NOT name this pipeline segment - so the sheet's own source does not actually support the row. However, the pipeline is real: offshore-technology.com/projects/haradh states 'Sweet and sour gas from the wells is transported through the Haradh manifold, located 12km from plant. The Waqr and Tinat manifolds are located 50km and 44km, respectively, from the plant. They carry sweet gas' and 'The gas is carried to the plant by five 20in and 30in gas transmission lines that total 130km'; Oil & Gas Journal (Haradh gas plant reaches capacity) independently describes the Tinat manifold 44km from the plant carrying sweet Khuff gas, with 87 wells feeding the plant via manifolds at Haradh, Waqr and Tinat. So a real ~44km line runs from the Tinat manifold (Tinat gas field, southern Ghawar/Unayzah reservoir, SE of the Haradh substructure) into the Haradh gas plant. NAME: 'Tinat Kuff' is a misspelling of 'Tinat Khuff' (the Khuff gas formation). CLASSIFICATION: source explicitly calls these 'gas transmission lines', so GEM's classification is defensible, but functionally this is a wellhead-manifold-to-plant gathering/collection line carrying RAW sweet Khuff wellhead gas to the Haradh plant (not processed sales gas on a trunk) - a caveat, not a reclassification. DUPLICATE: NOT a duplicate. Distinct from P1914 Waqr Khuff-Haradh (the Waqr manifold, 50km/30in) and from the Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah lines (P1917/P1918/P1919, Haradh->Hawiyah, 30in) - Tinat is its own manifold at 44km. The whole GEM cluster (Waqr/Tinat/Haradh-Hawiyah) derives from this same Haradh-plant five-line description; each maps to a distinct manifold/leg. GulfPub PE World Map has NO Tinat/Haradh/Khuff gathering line (it only carries the big MGS/East-West/Qatif-Berri trunks), consistent with this being smaller field infrastructure below GulfPub's coverage. SPEC: length 43km matches the sourced 44km (Tinat manifold distance) within 1km - good. Diameter 20in is one of the two diameters the source gives for the five lines (20in and 30in); GEM's per-line assignment (Tinat=20, Waqr=30) is a reasonable reading but the 20in is not pinned to Tinat by name - medium confidence, not clearly wrong. Capacity blank - no published per-line figure (plant total is 1.6 BSCFD). OWNER/OPERATOR: Saudi Aramco 100% - confirmed (Aramco owns/operates all Haradh gas gathering). FUEL: Gas (sweet Khuff gas) - confirmed. STATUS: operating - Haradh gas plant on stream since April 2003; confirmed operating.

routes.corridor_desc: Field-gathering line from the Tinat manifold to the Haradh Gas Plant, in the southern Al-Ahsa (Eastern Province) sector of the Greater Ghawar area, ~300km SW of Dhahran. Sources place the Tinat manifold 44km from the Haradh plant (vs GEM 43km); Tinat lies SE of the Haradh substructure over the Unayzah reservoir, so the corridor runs roughly SE-to-NW from the Tinat field into the plant. The Haradh plant endpoint is well-fixed (Haradh town/plant ~24.135N, 49.082E). The Tinat manifold end is only bounded to a ~44km radius arc SE of the plant - direction is inferred from 'immediately to the southeast' but the exact manifold coordinate is NOT sourced, so start_lat/lon left null. Loose corridor: a ~44km line trending SE from the Haradh plant within southern Ghawar.
routes.researcher_notes: End (Haradh Gas Plant) coordinate is defensible from the well-documented Haradh town/plant location (~24.135N, 49.082E, plant on stream April 2003). Start (Tinat manifold) not fabricated: only a distance (44km) and rough direction (SE of Haradh substructure) are sourced, so lat/lon left null and described in words. Suggested route accuracy LOWERED to 'low' relative to the current 'medium' because only one endpoint is fixed and the corridor is a distance/direction bound, not a mapped route.

summary: P1920 Tinat Kuff-Haradh: real gathering line (Tinat manifold ->Haradh plant, 44km, sweet Khuff gas), confirmed by offshore-technology + OGJ; owner Aramco, length, fuel, status all corroborated; caveats = name misspelling Kuff->Khuff, functionally field-gathering, diameter 20in only medium.
